q: When inspecting wood, how do you decide whether a stain is harmless or decay?
evidence: Examine all stains and discoloration carefully to determine whether or not they are harmless, or in a stage of preliminary or advanced decay.

q: Can a cracked wooden spar be repaired instead of replaced?
evidence: Cracked spars (except box spars) may be repaired by bonding plates of spruce or plywood of sufficient thickness to develop the longitudinal shear on both sides of the spar.

q: Are punch-type fabric testers FAA approved?
evidence: Mechanical devices used to test fabric by pressing against or piercing the finished fabric are not FAA approved and are used at the discretion of the mechanic to base an opinion on the general fabric condition.

q: Why is dope-proof paint applied over an organic coating before fabric is doped?
evidence: When doped fabrics are applied over an organic finished metal structure, the dope will have a tendency to loosen the finish on the metal.

q: What governs the seams when a large section of fabric is installed on a wing?
evidence: When installing large sections of fabric on a wing or other components, all machine-sewn and/or overlapped and doped seams should be made in accordance with the guidelines specified in paragraphs 2-7 and 2-8.

q: How can excessive moisture in a wood member be detected?
evidence: Moisture Meters are effective tools for detection of excessive moisture content in wood members.

q: What does a satisfactory bonded wood joint require of the adhesive film?
evidence: To produce this result, the bonding operation must be carefully controlled to obtain a continuous thin and uniform film of solid adhesive in the joint with adequate adhesion and penetration to both surfaces

q: Before repairing a damaged tubular member, what else must be inspected?
evidence: Prior to repairing tubular members, carefully examine the structure surrounding any visible damage to insure that no secondary damage remains undetected.

q: At what temperature do brazing and soldering differ?
evidence: Soldering is similar to brazing except that brazing materials normally melt at temperatures above 425 °C (800 °F), while solders melt at temperatures considerably lower.

q: Where are the minimum bend radii for aircraft plywood tabulated?
evidence: TABLE 1-2. Minimum recommended bend radii for aircraft plywood.

q: What precautions apply when handling hydraulic fluid?
evidence: In addition to any other instructions provided in the aircraft maintenance manual or by the fluid supplier, the following general precautions must be observed in the handling of hydraulic fluids:

q: What can cause banging and chattering noises in a hydraulic system?
evidence: Unusual noise in a hydraulic system, such as banging and chattering, may be caused by air or contamination in the system.

q: What defects should a tire inspection look for?
evidence: Tires should be inspected frequently for cuts, worn spots, bulges on the side walls, foreign bodies in the treads, and tread condition.

q: Why must welding on an engine mount be of the highest quality?
evidence: All welding on an engine mount must be of the highest quality, since vibration tends to accentuate any minor defect.

q: How should control cable tension be set?
evidence: control cable tension in accordance with the airframe manufacturer’s recommendations.

q: Which aluminum fuel tanks may be repaired by welding?
evidence: Welded or riveted fuel tanks that are made of commercially pure aluminum, 3003, 5052, or similar alloys, may be repaired by welding.

q: What should a periodic wheel inspection look for?
evidence: Inspect the wheels periodically for cracks, corrosion, dents, distortion, and faulty bearings in accordance with the manufacturer’s service information.

q: Can intergranular corrosion on a propeller blade be repaired in the field?
evidence: When intergranular corrosion is present, the repair can be properly accomplished only by an appropriately certificated propeller repair facility.

q: Why are acrylic windshields called lifetime windshields?
evidence: Acrylic windshields are often called “lifetime” windshields, to distinguish them from those made of the much shorter-lived acetate material.

q: Why should rivet heads not be removed with a cold chisel?
evidence: Removal of rivet heads with a cold chisel and hammer is not recommended because skin damage and distorted rivet holes will probably result.

q: A fatigue crack is suspected at the surface of an accessible part. Which inspection finds it with little part preparation?
evidence: If this surface is accessible, a high-frequency eddy current inspection can be performed with a minimum of part preparation and a high degree of sensitivity.

q: Why is magnetic particle inspection unsuitable for an aluminum fitting?
evidence: Magnetic particle inspection can be used only on ferro-magnetic materials (iron and steel).

q: Which method detects surface defects in nonmagnetic metals and in nonmetallic materials?
evidence: The penetrant method is effective for detecting surface defects in nonmagnetic metals and in a variety of nonmetallic materials.

q: Which instruments can test bonded structure for disbonds from one side?
evidence: Standard ultrasonic inspection instruments can be used for bond testing as previously noted; however, a wide variety of bond testing instruments are available for adaptation to specific bonded structure inspection problems.

q: What must the equipment list show for a special equipment item when its arm is unknown?
evidence: When the arm for such an item is not available, determine by actual measurement.

q: What should be checked where electrical arcing has left marks on conducting surfaces?
evidence: If there is evidence of electrical arcing, check for intermittent electrical contact between conducting surfaces, that may become a part of a ground plane or a current path.

q: What do the battery compartment venting tubes and attachments prevent?
evidence: Battery and battery compartment venting system tubes, nipples and attachments, when required, provide a means of avoiding the potential buildup of explosive gases

q: When must a pitot-static leak test be performed?
evidence: Such tests should be accomplished whenever a connection has been loosened or an instrument replaced.

q: What must a repair or refinish of a control surface avoid doing aft of the hinge line?
evidence: When repairing or refinishing control surfaces, especially on highperformance airplanes, care must be exercised that the repairs do not involve the addition of weight aft of the hinge line.

q: How are aluminum plate and sheet usually marked to show their grade?
evidence: Plate and sheet are usually marked with specification numbers or code markings in rows approximately 5 inches apart.

q: When repairing sheet metal, how should the rivet spacing and edge distance be chosen?
evidence: Unless structural deficiencies are suspected, the rivet spacing and edge distance should duplicate those of the original aircraft structure.

q: If the original rib lace spacing is not known, what maximum spacing may be used on the wings?
evidence: When the original lace spacing on the empennage surfaces and fuselage, is not known, a maximum spacing of two times the spacing shown in figure 2-12 for the slipstream area (prop wash) on the wings may be used.

q: What should be inspected in a battery compartment and around its vent?
evidence: Inspect battery compartment for electrolyte spillage, corrosion, and condition of protective paint.

q: Which rivets are used to join corrosion-resistant steel parts such as firewalls and exhaust stack brackets?
evidence: Corrosion-resistant steel rivets are used primarily in riveting corrosion-resistant steel parts such as firewalls, exhaust stack bracket attachments, and similar structures.

q: After a turnbuckle is adjusted, how must it be secured, and may the safety wire be reused?
evidence: Safety all turnbuckles with safety wire using either the double or single-wrap method, or with any appropriately approved special safetying device complying with the requirements of FAA Technical Standard Order TSO-C21.

q: What must be done to the wheel bearings before a wheel is installed on the axle?
evidence: The wheel bearings should be cleaned and packed with approved grease.

q: How often must the static system and each altimeter be inspected and tested for IFR operations?
evidence: Aircraft conducting operations in controlled airspace under instru ment flight rule (IFR) are required to have their static system(s) and each altimeter instrument inspected and tested within the previous 24 calendar months.

q: How is a pitot heater checked for proper operation?
evidence: Check the heater element or the entire tube for proper operation by noting either ammeter current or that the tube or port is hot to the touch.

q: When may 2017 or 2024 rivets be replaced with 2117 rivets?
evidence: It is acceptable to replace 2017 rivets of 3/16 inch diameter or less, and 2024 rivets of 5/32 inch diameter or less with 2117 rivets for general repairs, provided the replacement rivets are 1/32 inch greater in diameter than the rivets they replace.

q: What must be done before an air-oil shock strut is removed or disassembled?
evidence: Before an air-oil strut is removed or disassembled, the air valve should be opened to make sure that all air pressure is removed.

q: What defects should a general inspection of a fabric covering look for?
evidence: Loose finishing tape and reinforcing patches; chafing under fairings; brittle, cracking, peeling, or deteriorated coatings; fabric tears and rock damage; broken or missing rib lacing; and rodent nests are unacceptable.

q: How should rivets be arranged in a splice so the member does not fail at its outermost holes?
evidence: In general, arrange the rivets in the splice so that the design tensile load for the member and splice plate can be carried into the splice without failing the member at the outermost rivet holes.

q: What is the first step in removing corrosion from an aluminum part?
evidence: Positively identify the metal as aluminum.

q: Can a copper-sleeve splice replace a five-tuck splice in a control cable?
evidence: A patented process using copper sleeves may be used up to the full rated strength of the cable when the cable is looped around a thimble.

q: Why should a circuit breaker not be used as a switch?
evidence: Use of a circuit breaker as a switch is not recommended.

q: What should an antenna inspection check at its mounting base?
evidence: (10) Check the bonding of each antenna from mounting base to the aircraft skin.

q: When a wood spar splice is made where the routing is feathered, what plates go on first?
evidence: If splice is made where routing is feathered to full width of spar, tapered plates (conforming to the contour of the routing) should be added first; otherwise, the splice is the same as shown.

q: When is empty weight center of gravity computed with oil included?
evidence: EMPTY WEIGHT AND EMPTY WEIGHT CENTER OF GRAVITY (when aircraft is weighed with oil) GIVEN: Aircraft as weighed with full oil -------------------------------------------------------------- 1186 lbs.

q: Which engine case defects call for disassembling the gear train?
evidence: (a) Loose, sheared, or spalled cap screws or bolts.

q: Are rasped surfaces acceptable at the corners of a scarf patch?
evidence: Rasped surfaces, except at the corners of scarf patches and sawn surfaces, are not recommended as they are likely to be rough or inaccurate.

q: How should the viscosity of dope be set for coating fabric?
evidence: (5) The viscosity of the dope should be adjusted to uniformly wet the fabric, indicated by the fabric becoming translucent so that it penetrates through the fabric but does not drip or run down the opposite side.

q: How is pressure applied over a laminated plastic repair while it cures?
evidence: Apply pressure over the repair with tape or sandbags and allow it to cure.

q: Should propeller bolt threads be lubricated before torquing?
evidence: torquing procedures require all bolt threads to be dry, clean, and free of any lubrication before torquing.

q: Why does hydraulic system troubleshooting depend on the system's complexity?
evidence: Hydraulic system troubleshooting varies according to the complexity of the system and the components in the system.

q: What does minimum fuel mean in weight and balance?
evidence: Minimum fuel is the maximum amount of fuel which can be used in weight and balance computations when low fuel might adversely affect the most critical balance conditions.

q: Where are the detailed magneto-to-engine timing procedures found?
evidence: MAGNETO-TO-ENGINE TIMING. While the actual process of timing magnetos to an engine is covered in the engine manufacturer’s technical manuals, the following general procedures may be applied.

q: What should an electrical connector inspection look for?
evidence: Inspect electrical connectors for breaks in potting compound and corrosion of pins and wires.

q: What load may a swage-type terminal carry?
evidence: Swage-type terminals, manufactured in accordance with AN, are suitable for use in civil aircraft up to, and including, maximum cable loads.

q: What precaution keeps a repaired flight control surface from fluttering?
evidence: To prevent the occurrence of severe vibration or flutter of flight control surfaces during flight, precautions must be taken to stay within the design balance limitations when performing maintenance or repair.
